title: Unimodality of the independence sequence of a finite forest (Erdős Problem 993)
abstract: A Lean 4 and Mathlib formalization of the theorem that the independence sequence of every finite forest is unimodal: the numbers of independent sets with 0, 1, 2, ... vertices weakly increase up to some index and weakly decrease after it. This is the statement listed as Erdős Problem 993; later sources attribute the question to a 1987 paper of Alavi, Malde, Schwenk and Erdős. The first claimed proof for all finite forests is by T. Zhang and W. Li (self-archived preprints, September 2026). This repository formalizes a second proof, by W. Li, K. Vallier and T. Zhang: it adapts the public arXiv:2610.07943v1 and follows version 2.15 of that manuscript, deposited with restricted access and under revision. The Lean proof is computer-assisted and in two parts (at most 24 vertices; at least 25). About 13,700 finite computations are evaluated by the Lean kernel, without native_decide, on the three standard axioms. AI systems produced and reviewed all of the Lean; no human has read the Lean proofs. No manuscript cited is peer reviewed. No priority and no first formalization is claimed.
